role: wave 8, domain 8 (dense/sparse CC bombers, early INT86 heavy bombs), R4-fix
base: rev0 = V6nohunt (A 194 B sha 6861894f, B 202 B sha 8579e2c2)
idea: The only verified dangerous bomber in domain 8 is a page-lattice CC bomber tuned to the fixed anchor in-page offset 52h (B058 pg52: base 0.025). Every fixed lattice shift only moves the hole and costs on the field (B055/A011/B085). Fix tested here: a per-battle mixed lattice at zero bytes and zero turns. phoenix_init already does mov dx,[4A17h] followed by and dx,0 / or dx,0FFBh, so changing the immediates to and dx,3 / or dx,0FF8h makes FAR_SEG = 0FF8h..0FFBh from the low 2 bits of [4A17h]. That cell holds our B zombie_entry address (random per battle) and is read by A, B and captured zombies after round ~25, so the whole team picks the same lattice (22h/32h/42h/52h, p = 1/4 each). Geometry check: first-generation SP - anchor = gap + (10000h - 10h*FAR_SEG) = gap + 50h..80h stays = 0 mod 4 for all four values, so the A4 trigger still lands on the anchor; after generation 1, SP - anchor = 400h as before.

candidates.label: mix4 (per-battle mixed anchor lattice 22/32/42/52h)
candidates.change: A and B phoenix_init: and dx,0 -> and dx,3; or dx,0FFBh -> or dx,0FF8h (2 bytes changed per warrior). Zero bytes, zero turns.
candidates.notes: Works exactly as a mixed strategy: vs the static 52h bomber it recovers ~3/4 of the loss (+0.615), vs a static bomber on one of the new offsets it gives back ~1/4 (pg22 -0.175), and vs the all-offset bomber it changes little (+0.044). General cost on field S is not resolved (-0.002 +- 0.021); vs lattice-sensitive leaders it trades holes like the fixed shifts did (V6Guard +0.10, zchain4 -0.08, zrl03 -0.04). Main limitation: the coin is public. A 58-byte bomber that reads [4A17h] and bombs 22h+10h*([4A17h]&3) wipes mix4 (-0.547 vs base). So the worst case vs an informed attacker is unchanged. Not proposed for promotion: the threat it fixes does not exist in any field, and the general-cost interval is too wide.

counterCodes.name: B088_pgadapt
counterCodes.size: A 58 B sha 24c66cf9, B 59 B sha 58f3614b
counterCodes.what: B058 pg52 with an adaptive offset: waits ~10 rounds, reads [4A17h], bombs CCCCh at in-page 22h + 10h*([4A17h] and 3) of every page (partner 8000h later).
counterCodes.strength: vs mix4: candidate loses -0.547 vs base (mvmvo, 0/8); against rev0 it hits only 1/4 of battles. Use it against any future base that derives its lattice from a public cell.

threatFindings.threat: A static page-lattice CC bomber tuned to in-page 52h wipes rev0; a per-battle mixed lattice (zero bytes) recovers most of it
threatFindings.evidence: 52phq: B058_pg52 +0.615 [0.542,0.687] 8/0 for mix4 vs rev0; bomber team score drops 0.166 -> 0.044.
threatFindings.impact: Large vs this purpose-built probe only; no field warrior targets 52h (B058, B068).

threatFindings.threat: The mixed lattice opens holes at the other offsets (mixed-strategy trade)
threatFindings.impact: Any single-offset static bomber now gets ~1/4 of its maximum; same total exposure, spread out.

threatFindings.threat: The all-offset (2 mod 10h) bomber still hurts with a mixed lattice
threatFindings.impact: The architectural hole (1-byte critical anchor dwelling 256/512 rounds) stays; only lattice-specific attackers are affected.

threatFindings.threat: An adaptive bomber that reads the public [4A17h] cell defeats the mixed lattice
threatFindings.evidence: mvmvo: B088_pgadapt -0.547 [-0.701,-0.393] 0/8 for mix4 vs rev0 (rev0 at fixed 52h is hit in only 1/4 of battles).
threatFindings.impact: Worst case vs an informed attacker is not improved. A private coin (team-shared memory: B stosw at instr 1; A push es ... pop ds; mov dx,[0]) would cost 2-3 turns and is untested; a trail-scanning bomber (domain 7) could still find the lattice.

threatFindings.threat: Lattice choice changes results vs lattice-sensitive leaders
threatFindings.impact: Net about 0 over the four leaders (+0.010), but cohort-level trades like the fixed shifts (B055, A011).

threatFindings.threat: Real 2025 CC bombers (R1DDLE dense sweep, tson 13-step) depend on our lattice
threatFindings.impact: None; these bombers are lattice-blind, as expected from their stride.

threatFindings.threat: A late [4A17h] writer splits A and B (or captured zombies) onto different lattices under mix4
threatFindings.evidence: Static: all known writers (V6 family, B073/B083 poisoners) write before round 5; A and B read it around rounds 30-35. Not tested.
threatFindings.impact: Probably rare; would add partner crossfire in those battles.

threatFindings.threat: Early INT86 heavy bombs before we leave the load image
threatFindings.evidence: Not re-tested here; B058 trace pkj3o and B068 ogq11 (~-0.007 per bomb). Bombs land at turns 5-8, before any startup can finish; only image size matters (C2/stripA already shrink A).
threatFindings.impact: No defense bytes justified; no job spent.

recommendation: Do not promote mix4. It is a working zero-byte, zero-turn defense against a static 52h page-lattice bomber (+0.615) with no measurable field cost on the screen (-0.002 +- 0.021), but it only spreads the exposure (pg22 -0.175), leaves the all-offset bomber in place (+0.044), trades leader cohorts (V6Guard +0.10 vs zchain4 -0.08), and a 58-byte bomber reading the public [4A17h] cell defeats it (-0.547). The threat it answers does not exist in any field. Keep it documented as a cheap option if a 52h-targeting opponent appears; if pursued, use a private team-shared coin and re-test vs B088_pgadapt and B058_pgall16.
notes: The coin reuses the dead mov dx,[4A17h] in phoenix_init, so it conflicts with A022 SD/SDd and K (which delete that read). Captured zombies read the same cell in B's phoenix_init and so share the lattice.
